# Yamaha Engagement: Role Plan

## What This Role Is

You are the **single point of accountability** between Yamaha Music Innovation Fund and all of Sedin's internal units. Your job has two layers:

1. **External:** Be the face, voice, and conscience of the entire engagement for Yamaha
2. **Internal:** Force coherence across Code Rapper, Data Culture, Marketing, and Tarka Labs before anything touches the client

The existential risk: Yamaha sees four vendors in a trenchcoat. The win condition: they see one high-trust partner who happens to have deep benches.

---

## The June Deadline First

**Yamaha needs to see value by end of June.** Everything else is secondary to this.

Immediate actions this week:
- Define precisely what "value" means to Yamaha's 4-person team — ask them directly, in writing. Do they want a live Creator Pass milestone? A data dashboard? A roadmap? Get this in writing so you can deliver exactly that, not your interpretation.
- Map what each internal team has that is shippable or demonstrable by June 30.
- Pick 1-2 things that are genuinely impressive and sequence everything else behind them. Do not try to show everything.
- Create a June delivery brief (1 page max) and share internally so all four teams are building toward the same finish line.

---

## Daily Operating Rhythm

### Morning (30 min)

| Activity | Why |
|---|---|
| Scan all Yamaha threads/email | Nothing surprises you in client calls |
| Read yesterday's async updates from each team | Know blockers before they fester |
| Identify the one thing that could go wrong today | Fix it before it becomes a client issue |

### Core Day

**Internal (keep short, keep tight):**
- One async written standup from each department lead — not a meeting, a written 3-liner: _what shipped, what's next, any blockers_
- You synthesize these into one coherent picture
- Escalate blockers before EOD, not tomorrow

**External (deliberate, controlled):**
- All Yamaha communication routes through you
- If another team member needs to communicate directly, you are CC'd and have pre-approved the message
- Respond to Yamaha within 2 hours during business hours — speed of response signals confidence

### End of Day (15 min)

- Update your running delivery tracker (see below)
- Flag anything Yamaha asked for that does not yet have an owner assigned
- Send one brief proactive note to Yamaha if something good shipped — don't wait for the weekly call

---

## Weekly Rhythm

| Day | Activity |
|---|---|
| Monday | Internal sync with all department leads. Review the week's commitments vs. reality gap. |
| Wednesday | Written status update to Yamaha (3-5 bullets: what shipped, what's next, any decisions needed from them) |
| Friday | Yamaha call (or async loom if they prefer). You present. One voice. |
| Friday | Internal retro: what client comms went sideways, what coordination failed, fix the process |

---

## Communication Framework

### The Cardinal Rule

**Yamaha should never see the seams between Sedin departments.**

This means:
- One Slack channel or email thread with Yamaha, owned by you
- Departments do not CC Yamaha on inter-team coordination
- If there is disagreement internally, it is resolved before Yamaha hears anything
- All commitments to Yamaha are made by you — departments can say things informally but only you commit timelines

### The "One Team" Narrative

In every Yamaha touchpoint, use "we" not "our Tarka Labs team" or "our data team." Reference capabilities not org structure: "we have deep expertise in X" not "our data science division."

Prepare a one-paragraph team introduction for any new Yamaha stakeholder that introduces the team as a single integrated unit.

### Escalation Protocol

If a department is going to miss a commitment:
1. You find out as early as possible (daily standup habit)
2. You tell Yamaha before the deadline, not after, and with a revised plan already in hand
3. You own the message — no "our marketing team dropped the ball"

---

## Internal Coordination Model

### Your Relationship with Each Department Lead

Treat each lead as your delivery partner for their domain. Establish:
- A weekly 30-min 1:1 with each
- A shared tracker they update (not a meeting, a doc)
- Clear ownership: they own how, you own what and when with the client

### The One Pager

Create a single internal brief called **Yamaha Engagement Overview** covering:
- What we've committed to and by when
- Who owns each workstream (by department)
- What Yamaha's success criteria look like
- What we must not say / surface to the client (internal tensions, org structure, billing disputes)

Every new person touching this engagement reads this before they email or call anyone at Yamaha.

### Preventing the "Many Vendors" Problem

The trap is that each department defaults to their own branding, tools, and communication style. Your job is to harmonize:
- One slide deck template for all Yamaha presentations
- One tone of voice (professional, capable, collaborative)
- One project board/tracker that all teams update — Yamaha can have read access to this if it builds trust

---

## Delivery Tracker

Maintain a living document with these columns:

| Commitment | Made On | Promised By | Owner (internal) | Status | Yamaha Notified? |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Creator Pass checkout fix | May 12 | May 19 | Tarka Labs | Done | Yes |
| ... | | | | | |

Review this weekly. Any row where "Owner" is blank is a fire.

---

## Proving the Model (So It Repeats)

The meta-objective: prove Sedin can operate as a unified technology partner at the $1M+ level. To document this for future clients:
- Keep a running log of what worked and what didn't in this engagement
- After June (assuming billing unlocks), write a one-page internal case study: how we delivered, what the client valued, what we'd do differently
- This becomes the playbook for the next Yamaha-type client

---

## What Success Looks Like

**By end of June:** Yamaha renews or expands the engagement. They reference you by name as the person who "gets it."

**By Q3:** Yamaha stops comparing you to what they could have built internally. You are their default answer to "we need to build something."

**Long term:** This engagement is cited internally as the proof case for Sedin's unified partner model.
